rules.title: Security Deposit Law maximum deposit and annual increase limit
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent. Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.
rules.key_value: one and one-half (1.5) times one month's rent; yearly increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes, where the landlord collects a security deposit.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are excepted, but a tenant in such a dwelling may make the Security Deposit Law applicable to their tenancy 30 days after sending a written request to the landlord. Landlords are not required to collect a security deposit.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

rules.title: Pet security deposit limit
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge a pet security deposit if, combined with the regular security deposit, it exceeds one and one-half times one month's rent.
rules.key_value: pet deposit plus regular deposit may not exceed one and one-half (1.5) times one month's rent
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes, where the landlord collects a security deposit.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are excepted, but a tenant in such a dwelling may make the Security Deposit Law applicable to their tenancy 30 days after sending a written request to the landlord.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord may not charge a pet security deposit if it exceeds one and one-half times one month’s rent when combined with the regular security deposit.

rules.title: Return of security deposit after lease termination under the Safe Housing Act
rules.requirement: When a tenant terminates a lease early under the Safe Housing Act due to domestic violence, the landlord must make the security deposit plus interest available within 15 business days after termination and notify the tenant in writing within three business days of when and where to pick it up, with a duplicate notice to the relocation officer or municipal clerk. The deposit must be available for thirty (30) days during normal business hours in the municipality, accompanied by an itemized list of interest and deductions.
rules.key_value: return within 15 business days; written notice within three (3) business days; available for thirty (30) days
rules.coverage_text: Tenants who terminate a lease before its expiration as victims of domestic violence under the New Jersey Safe Housing Act.
rules.exemptions: This law does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.
rules.quoted_span: Within 15 business days after the lease  is terminated, the landlord shall make available the return of the tenant’s security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant’s agent. In addition, within three business days after the lease is terminated, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of when and where the tenant can pick up the security deposit.
